_howto: One item per paper figure/table (or panel group). This file is the machine-readable coverage contract:
decision for numeric items: target (with target_ids) | deferred_blocked (with blocker).
decision for non_numeric items: excluded | target.
Allowed blockers: missing_author_data, missing_benchmark_metadata, missing_source_input, insufficient_compute, requires_external_hardware, covered_by_target, user_descoped.
'Supporting', 'low priority', or 'similar to another figure' are NOT blockers: reproduce the item instead.
Coverage means scientific reproduction (independent numerics or analytic references). Digitized curves and copied source panels do not count as coverage.
If scientific input is missing, deferred_blocked with evidence is an honest partial state.

If execution is compute/hardware-limited or a mapped target is reduced_scale, add a code-ready implementation contract: status=ready, case-local code_refs, config config_ref, working_directory=workspace, argv-style entrypoint, expected_outputs, and acceptance_criteria.
Put reusable contracts in top-level implementations and reference them from items with implementation_ref; an inline implementation object is also accepted.
Compute may postpone execution; it may not postpone writing runnable code.

acceptance_criteria: All six numerical panels use N=20, the printed Hamiltonians, explicit initial states, and the complete plotted time range.
The SU(2) numerical largest eigenvalue agrees with Main Eq. (8) on its stated early-time validity interval.
The SU(4) run reproduces six SQL eigenvalues at tau=0, a leading maximum near 146, and the three printed pi/4 eigenvalue anchors.
Dense and sparse evolution agree on smaller systems, and every QFIM is positive semidefinite within tolerance.
Degenerate optimal-generator vectors are assessed through their projectors; source pixels never select an eigenvector gauge.
The isolated runner reads no raw paper, TeX, authored figure, comparison image, author code, or author array.
